raw_case_text:
A 69-year-old male farmer with no prior medical history was admitted to a local hospital after experiencing fever for 5 days and dyspnea with hemoptysis for 1 day. He had a history of exposure to poultry manure while working on his farm 5 days prior. Chest computed tomography (CT) revealed pulmonary infection and interstitial changes (Figure 1A). The primary diagnosis was severe pneumonia and acute respiratory failure, and the patient was placed on mechanical ventilation via endotracheal intubation. However, his oxygen saturation continued to deteriorate, and bloody sputum was aspirated from his airway. Twenty hours after intubation, he was transferred to our emergency intensive care unit (EICU).
Upon arrival at the EICU, the patient was in a sedated and analgesic state, with a body temperature of 36.8 C, respiratory rate of 17 breaths/min, pulse rate of 138 beats/min, and blood pressure of 137/90 mmHg (with norepinephrine infusion at 0.5 mug/kg/min). Oxygen saturation was 88%. He remained on mechanical ventilation in volume-controlled mode with a tidal volume of 350 mL, an FiO2 of 100%, and a positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP) of 15 cmH2O (1 mmH2O = 0.098 kPa). A large amount of fresh red bloody sputum was aspirated from the airway, and extensive moist rales were heard in both lungs. Laboratory results showed: P/F, 85 mmHg; Platelet count (PLT), 43 x 109/L; C-reactive protein (CRP), 213.74 mg/L; Procalcitonin (PCT), >100 ng/mL; Activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT), 36.8 s; Myoglobin (MYO), >2000 ng/mL; Creatinine (CR), 240 mg/dL; Alanine aminotransferase (ALT), 111 U/L; Total bilirubin (TBIL), 70 mumol/L. The primary diagnosis included severe pneumonia, DAH, severe ARDS, septic shock, and hepatic and renal dysfunction.
Despite optimized mechanical ventilation, his P/F remained below 80 mmHg for over 3 h. VV-ECMO and CRRT support were initiated, along with intermittent prone ventilation. Mechanical ventilation was switched to pressure control mode (inspiratory pressure 12 cmH2O, tidal volume 150-350 mL, PEEP 15 cmH2O, plateau pressure <=30 mmHg). Empirical antibiotic therapy included piperacillin-tazobactam (4.5 g every 8 h) combined with omadacycline (100 mg daily, initial dose 200 mg IV). The patient also received methylprednisolone (200 mg IV) for anti-inflammatory treatment, recombinant human thrombopoietin (15,000 U SC daily) to increase platelet count, platelet transfusion (10 U), fresh plasma, packed red blood cells, and norepinephrine (0.1-0.8 mug/kg/min) for blood pressure support. Bronchoscopic alveolar lavage was performed, and both blood and lavage fluid were sent for mNGS testing. Unfractionated heparin (UFH) anticoagulation was initiated at the 5th hour of VV-ECMO operation. On day 3, mNGS confirmed Leptospira interrogans infection, with a coverage rate of 1% and a relative abundance of 16.45% (Figure 1D). On day 5, VV-ECMO was discontinued, and omadacycline was stopped. Follow-up chest CT showed improvement in pulmonary hemorrhage compared to before (Figure 1B). The endotracheal tube was removed on day 6, the patient was transferred out of the EICU on day 9, and was discharged after recovery on day 20. A follow-up chest CT before discharge showed that pulmonary hemorrhage had significantly improved (Figure 1C). The treatment process is summarized in Figure 1E, and the trends in blood test results are detailed in Table 1. Changes in ventilator parameters, ECMO parameters, and medication dosages during ECMO are detailed in Table 2.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 69-year-old male farmer presented with a 5-day history of fever and a 1-day history of dyspnea and hemoptysis.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Five days after exposure to poultry manure on his farm, the patient developed fever, followed 4 days later by acute dyspnea and hemoptysis. He was admitted to a local hospital with pulmonary infiltrates on chest CT and intubated for acute respiratory failure, but persistent severe hypoxemia and copious bloody airway secretions prompted transfer 20 hours later to the emergency intensive care unit (EICU).
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously healthy farmer with no prior medical history; exposed to poultry manure while farming 5 days prior to symptom onset.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, dyspnea, and hemoptysis.

objective.physical_examination: On EICU arrival (sedated, intubated on volume-controlled ventilation [VT 350 mL, FiO2 100%, PEEP 15 cmH2O], on norepinephrine 0.5 µg/kg/min): temperature 36.8 °C, respiratory rate 17 breaths/min, pulse 138 beats/min, blood pressure 137/90 mmHg, and SpO2 88%. Large amounts of fresh red bloody sputum were aspirated from the endotracheal tube, and chest auscultation revealed extensive bilateral moist rales.
objective.routine_investigations: EICU admission labs: PaO2/FiO2 ratio 85 mmHg (falling to <80 mmHg over 3 hours), platelets 43 × 10⁹/L, CRP 213.74 mg/L, procalcitonin >100 ng/mL, aPTT 36.8 s, myoglobin >2,000 ng/mL, serum creatinine 240 µmol/L (reported as 240 mg/dL in text), ALT 111 U/L, and total bilirubin 70 µmol/L.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial chest CT showed bilateral pulmonary infection and interstitial changes. Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) and peripheral blood metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) performed on day 3 confirmed Leptospira interrogans (1% genome coverage, 16.45% relative abundance). Serial follow-up chest CT scans on day 5 and prior to discharge demonstrated progressive resolution of diffuse alveolar hemorrhage.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed severe pulmonary hemorrhagic leptospirosis complicated by diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (DAH), severe ARDS, septic shock, and hepatorenal dysfunction, confirmed by blood and BALF mNGS identifying Leptospira interrogans. Managed with VV-ECMO (with delayed unfractionated heparin anticoagulation starting at hour 5), continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT), prone positioning, lung-protective pressure-controlled ventilation, empiric IV piperacillin-tazobactam (4.5 g q8h) plus IV omadacycline (200 mg loading dose, then 100 mg daily), IV methylprednisolone (200 mg), subcutaneous recombinant human thrombopoietin (15,000 U daily), blood product transfusions (10 U platelets, FFP, PRBCs), and norepinephrine (0.1–0.8 µg/kg/min). VV-ECMO and omadacycline were discontinued on day 5, the patient was extubated on day 6, transferred from the EICU on day 9, and discharged home recovered on day 20.
